subject: math
title: Money and Making Change: Canadian Coins, Bills and Counting Up
seo_title: Grade 3 Money Worksheets: Canadian Coins and Making Change (Ontario)
standard_text: Estimate and calculate the change required for various simple cash transactions involving whole-dollar amounts and amounts of less than one dollar
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 math worksheets on money: name Canadian coins and bills, count nickels, dimes, quarters, loonies and toonies, make amounts in different ways, and make change from $1, $5, $10 and $20 by counting up. Snack sale and book fair word problems, 100 questions with an answer key. Follows the Ontario curriculum and helps with EQAO practice.
key_big: To make change, count up from the price to the money paid.
key_sub: For 65¢ paid with a loonie: 65¢ to 70¢ is 5¢, 70¢ to $1 is 30¢, so the change is 35¢. Count coins by value, not size: the small dime (10¢) is worth more than the bigger nickel (5¢).
body_html:
Canadian coins and bills

Know each coin by its name and its value. Size does not tell you the value: the dime is the smallest coin, but it is worth more than the nickel.

CoinValueGood to know
nickel5¢2 nickels = 1 dime
dime10¢10 dimes = $1
quarter25¢4 quarters = $1
loonie$111 sides, gold colour
toonie$22 loonies = 1 toonie

Count the money, biggest first

Put the coins in order, biggest value first. Then count on.

Example

Count a $5 bill, 2 toonies and a loonie.

$5, then $7, $9, then $10.

Answer: $10

Make the same amount in different ways

50¢ can be 25¢ + 25¢, or 25¢ + 10¢ + 10¢ + 5¢, or 5 dimes. For the fewest coins, use the biggest coin you can each time.

Make change by counting up

Start at the price. Count up to the next 10¢, then to $1. Add the jumps. For whole dollars, count up to the next $10, then to the money paid.

Example

A pair of mitts costs $8. Pay with a $20 bill. What is the change?

$8 + $2 = $10. $10 + $10 = $20. $2 + $10 = $12. Check: $8 + $12 = $20.

Answer: $12

Estimate first. 45¢ is about 50¢, so the change from $1 is about 50¢. The exact change is 55¢.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The nickel is bigger, so it is worth moreRead the value: the small dime is 10¢, the nickel is 5¢
4 coins, so 4¢Count the value of each coin: 25¢, 50¢, 60¢, 65¢
A quarter is 20¢A quarter is 25¢. Four quarters make $1
Change from $1 for 65¢ is 45¢Count up: 65¢ + 5¢ = 70¢, 70¢ + 30¢ = $1. The change is 35¢
The change is the priceThe change is what you get back: price + change = money paid

faq.q: What do Grade 3 students learn about money in Ontario?
faq.a: In the Ontario math curriculum (Financial Literacy, F1.1), Grade 3 students estimate and calculate the change for simple cash purchases, using whole-dollar amounts and amounts under $1. They also name Canadian coins and bills and count collections of money.

faq.q: Why are there no pennies in Canada?
faq.a: Canada stopped giving out pennies in 2013. When you pay with cash, the total is rounded to the nearest 5¢, so the nickel is the smallest coin students count.

faq.q: How do you teach making change in Grade 3?
faq.a: Count up from the price to the money paid: for 65¢ from $1, go 65¢ to 70¢ (5¢), then 70¢ to $1 (30¢), so the change is 35¢. Then check that price + change = money paid.

faq.q: Is money on the Grade 3 EQAO math test?
faq.a: The Grade 3 EQAO math assessment is based on the Ontario math curriculum, which includes Financial Literacy. Counting money and making change also practises the adding and subtracting skills students need for the test.

sets.title: Coins and bills: names and values

items.q: What is the name of this coin?
items.e: This is a loonie. It is gold in colour, has 11 sides and is worth $1.

items.q: What is the name of this coin?
items.e: This is a toonie. It has a silver ring and a gold centre and is worth $2. Loonie is $1, toonie is $2.

items.q: What is the name of this coin?
items.e: This is a dime, worth 10¢. It is the smallest coin, but it is worth more than a nickel.

items.q: What is the name of this coin?
items.e: This is a nickel, worth 5¢. It is bigger than a dime, but worth less.

items.q: What is the name of this coin?
items.e: This is a quarter, worth 25¢. Four quarters make $1.

items.q: How much is a quarter worth?
items.e: A quarter is worth 25¢. It is not 20¢: four quarters make 100¢, and 4 × 25¢ = 100¢.

items.q: How much is a dime worth?
items.e: A dime is worth 10¢. Ten dimes make $1. The nickel (5¢) is bigger, but the dime is worth more.

items.q: How much is a nickel worth?
items.e: A nickel is worth 5¢. Two nickels make a dime.

items.q: How much is a loonie worth?
items.e: A loonie is worth $1 (100¢). The toonie is the $2 coin.

items.q: How much is a toonie worth?
items.e: A toonie is worth $2. It is worth the same as two loonies.

items.q: Which coin has 11 sides?
items.e: The loonie has 11 sides and is gold in colour. The other coins are round.

items.q: The nickel is bigger than the dime. Which coin is worth more?
items.e: The dime is worth 10¢. The nickel is worth 5¢. Size does not tell you the value.

items.q: Which coin is worth the least?
items.e: Nickel 5¢, dime 10¢, quarter 25¢, loonie $1. The nickel is worth the least, even though the dime is smaller.

items.q: How many nickels make a dime?
items.e: A dime is 10¢ and a nickel is 5¢. 5¢ + 5¢ = 10¢, so 2 nickels make a dime.

items.q: How many nickels make a quarter?
items.e: Count by 5s to 25: 5¢, 10¢, 15¢, 20¢, 25¢. That is 5 nickels. 4 nickels make only 20¢.

items.q: How many quarters make $1?
items.e: Count by 25s: 25¢, 50¢, 75¢, 100¢. 100¢ = $1, so 4 quarters. 5 would be right only if a quarter were 20¢.

items.q: How many dimes make $1?
items.e: Count by 10s: 10¢, 20¢, 30¢ … 100¢. That is 10 dimes.

items.q: How many cents are in $1?
items.e: $1 = 100 cents. That is why 4 quarters (4 × 25¢) or 10 dimes (10 × 10¢) make $1.

items.q: How many loonies make a toonie?
items.e: A loonie is $1 and a toonie is $2. $1 + $1 = $2, so 2 loonies make a toonie.

items.q: How many $5 bills make $20?
items.e: Count by 5s: $5, $10, $15, $20. That is 4 bills. 15 comes from 20 − 5.

items.q: How much money is shown?
items.e: Each dime is 10¢. Count by 10¢: 10¢, 20¢, 30¢, 40¢. That is 40¢. Count the value of each coin, not the number of coins.

items.q: Noah has these coins. How much does he have?
items.e: Each nickel is 5¢. Count by 5¢: 5¢, 10¢, 15¢, 20¢, 25¢, 30¢. That is 30¢. Count the value of each coin, not the number of coins.

items.q: Nathan finds these coins in his backpack. How much is it?
items.e: Each quarter is 25¢. Count by 25¢: 25¢, 50¢, 75¢. That is 75¢. Count the value of each coin, not the number of coins.

items.q: What is the total?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin and count on: 25¢, 35¢, 45¢. That is 45¢.

items.q: Mei puts this money in a piggy bank. How much is in the bank?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin and count on: 10¢, 20¢, 30¢, 35¢. That is 35¢.

items.q: How much money is shown?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin and count on: 25¢, 50¢, 60¢, 65¢. That is 65¢.

items.q: Leah has these coins. How much does she have?
items.e: Put the money in order, biggest value first. Start with the biggest coin and count on: 25¢, 35¢, 40¢, 45¢, 50¢. That is 50¢.

items.q: Arjun finds these coins in his backpack. How much is it?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin and count on: 25¢, 35¢, 45¢, 55¢. That is 55¢.

items.q: What is the total?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin and count on: 25¢, 35¢, 45¢, 55¢, 65¢, 70¢. That is 70¢.

items.q: Jayden puts this money in a piggy bank. How much is in the bank?
items.e: Put the money in order, biggest value first. Start with the biggest coin and count on: 25¢, 50¢, 60¢, 70¢, 80¢, 85¢. That is 85¢.

items.q: How much money is shown?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin and count on: 25¢, 50¢, 75¢, 85¢, 90¢, 95¢. That is 95¢.

items.q: Owen has these coins. How much does he have?
items.e: Put the money in order, biggest value first. Start with the biggest coin and count on: 25¢, 50¢, 60¢, 70¢, 80¢, 90¢. That is 90¢.

items.q: Hana finds these coins in her backpack. How much is it?
items.e: Put the money in order, biggest value first. Start with the biggest coin: 25¢, 50¢, 75¢, 85¢, 95¢, 100¢. 100¢ = $1.

items.q: What is the total?
items.e: Each loonie is $1. Count by $1: $1, $2, $3. That is $3.

items.q: Aiden puts this money in a piggy bank. How much is in the bank?
items.e: Each toonie is $2. Count by $2: $2, $4, $6. That is $6.

items.q: How much money is shown?
items.e: Count the dollars, biggest first: $2, $4, $5. That is $5.

items.q: Benjamin has these coins. How much does he have?
items.e: Put the money in order, biggest value first. Count the dollars, biggest first: $2, $4, $6, $7, $8. That is $8.

items.q: Liam puts this money in a piggy bank. How much is in the bank?
items.e: Put the money in order, biggest value first. Count the dollars, biggest first: $5, $7, $9, $10. That is $10.

items.q: What is the total?
items.e: Count the dollars, biggest first: $10, $15, $17. That is $17.

items.q: Ava puts this money in a piggy bank. How much is in the bank?
items.e: Put the money in order, biggest value first. Count the dollars, biggest first: $20, $30, $35, $36, $37. That is $37.

items.q: Which coins make 35¢?
Which coins make 50¢?
Which is worth the same as this money?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin and count on: 5¢, 10¢. That is 10¢. So one dime is worth the same.

items.q: Which is worth the same as this money?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin: 25¢, 50¢, 75¢, 100¢. 100¢ = $1. So one loonie is worth the same.

items.q: Which is worth the same as this money?
items.e: Count the dollars, biggest first: $1, $2. That is $2. So one toonie is worth the same.

items.q: What is the fewest coins you can use to make 30¢?
items.e: Use the biggest coin you can each time: 25¢, 5¢ = 30¢. That is 2 coins. There is no 30¢ coin, so 1 coin is not possible. Three dimes work, but 2 coins is fewer.

items.q: Which of these does not make 60¢?
items.e: 25¢, 25¢, 5¢ = 55¢, not 60¢. The others all make 60¢.

items.q: Kai has 3 coins. Together they make 45¢. Which coins does he have?
Which coins make 75¢?
Which uses the fewest coins to make 40¢?
items.e: All of these make 40¢. 25¢, 10¢, 5¢ uses only 3 coins: start with the biggest one you can.

items.q: What is the fewest coins you can use to make 65¢?
items.e: Use the biggest coin you can each time: 25¢, 25¢, 10¢, 5¢ = 65¢. That is 4 coins. Three coins can make 60¢ or 75¢, but not 65¢. Six dimes and a nickel is 7 coins.

items.q: Priya has 4 coins. Together they make 70¢. Which coins does she have?
Which of these does not make $1?
Which coins make 90¢?
Which coins make $3?
Which of these does not make $5?
items.e: $2, $2, $2 = $6, not $5. The others all make $5.

items.q: Which is worth the same as this money?
items.e: Count the dollars, biggest first: $2, $4, $6, $8, $10. That is $10. So one $10 bill is worth the same.

items.q: What is the fewest coins you can use to make $7?
items.e: Use the biggest coin you can each time: $2, $2, $2, $1 = $7. That is 4 coins. Seven loonies work, but that is 7 coins. Three toonies make only $6.

items.q: Which uses the fewest bills to make $35?
items.e: All of these make $35. $20, $10, $5 uses only 3 bills: start with the biggest one you can.

items.q: Olivia has 3 bills. Together they make $25. Which bills does she have?
Emma buys a pen for 65¢. She pays with a loonie. How much change does she get? Count up on the number line.
items.e: Count up from 65¢ to $1: 65¢ + 5¢ = 70¢, 70¢ + 30¢ = $1. Add the jumps: 5¢ + 30¢ = 35¢. The change is 35¢. Check: 65¢ + 35¢ = $1.

items.q: Chloe buys an eraser for 40¢. She pays with a loonie. How much change does she get?
items.e: Count up from 40¢ to $1: 40¢ + 60¢ = $1. The change is 60¢. Check: 40¢ + 60¢ = $1.

items.q: Noah buys a bottle of water for 85¢. He pays with a loonie. How much change does he get? Count up on the number line.
items.e: Count up from 85¢ to $1: 85¢ + 5¢ = 90¢, 90¢ + 10¢ = $1. Add the jumps: 5¢ + 10¢ = 15¢. The change is 15¢. Check: 85¢ + 15¢ = $1.

items.q: Nathan buys a bag of pretzels for 55¢. He pays with a loonie. How much change does he get?
items.e: Count up from 55¢ to $1: 55¢ + 5¢ = 60¢, 60¢ + 40¢ = $1. Add the jumps: 5¢ + 40¢ = 45¢. The change is 45¢. Check: 55¢ + 45¢ = $1.

items.q: Mateo buys a sticker for 20¢. He pays with a loonie. How much change does he get?
items.e: Count up from 20¢ to $1: 20¢ + 80¢ = $1. The change is 80¢. Check: 20¢ + 80¢ = $1.

items.q: Mei buys a pencil topper for 35¢. She pays with a loonie. How much change does she get? Count up on the number line.
items.e: Count up from 35¢ to $1: 35¢ + 5¢ = 40¢, 40¢ + 60¢ = $1. Add the jumps: 5¢ + 60¢ = 65¢. The change is 65¢. Check: 35¢ + 65¢ = $1.

items.q: Amira buys a notepad for 70¢. She pays with a loonie. How much change does she get?
items.e: Count up from 70¢ to $1: 70¢ + 30¢ = $1. The change is 30¢. Check: 70¢ + 30¢ = $1.

items.q: Leah buys a glue stick for 45¢. She pays with a loonie. How much change does she get?
items.e: Count up from 45¢ to $1: 45¢ + 5¢ = 50¢, 50¢ + 50¢ = $1. Add the jumps: 5¢ + 50¢ = 55¢. The change is 55¢. Check: 45¢ + 55¢ = $1.

items.q: Arjun buys a ruler for 90¢. He pays with a loonie. How much change does he get?
items.e: Count up from 90¢ to $1: 90¢ + 10¢ = $1. The change is 10¢. Check: 90¢ + 10¢ = $1.

items.q: Maya buys a balloon for 15¢. She pays with a loonie. How much change does she get?
items.e: Count up from 15¢ to $1: 15¢ + 5¢ = 20¢, 20¢ + 80¢ = $1. Add the jumps: 5¢ + 80¢ = 85¢. The change is 85¢. Check: 15¢ + 85¢ = $1.

items.q: A bag of crackers costs 45¢. Jayden pays with a loonie. About how much change will he get?
items.e: 45¢ is close to 50¢. $1 − 50¢ = 50¢, so the change is about 50¢. (Exactly: 45¢ + 55¢ = $1.)

items.q: Zoe buys a skipping rope for $3. She pays with a $5 bill. How much change does she get?
items.e: Count up from $3 to $5: $3 + $2 = $5. The change is $2. Check: $3 + $2 = $5.

items.q: Owen buys a pack of hockey cards for $6. He pays with a $10 bill. How much change does he get?
items.e: Count up from $6 to $10: $6 + $4 = $10. The change is $4. Check: $6 + $4 = $10. Count the jumps from $6. Do not count $6 itself: that gives $5.

items.q: Hana buys a flying disc for $7. She pays with a $10 bill. How much change does she get? Count up on the number line.
items.e: Count up from $7 to $10: $7 + $3 = $10. The change is $3. Check: $7 + $3 = $10. Count the jumps from $7. Do not count $7 itself: that gives $4.

items.q: Ethan buys a soccer ball for $13. He pays with a $20 bill. How much change does he get? Count up on the number line.
items.e: Count up from $13 to $20: $13 + $7 = $20. The change is $7. Check: $13 + $7 = $20. Count the jumps from $13. Do not count $13 itself: that gives $8.

items.q: Aiden buys a pair of mitts for $8. He pays with a $20 bill. How much change does he get? Count up on the number line.
items.e: Count up from $8 to $20: $8 + $2 = $10, $10 + $10 = $20. Add the jumps: $2 + $10 = $12. The change is $12. Check: $8 + $12 = $20. Count the jumps from $8. Do not count $8 itself: that gives $13.

items.q: Lucas buys a board game for $15. He pays with a $20 bill. How much change does he get?
items.e: Count up from $15 to $20: $15 + $5 = $20. The change is $5. Check: $15 + $5 = $20. Count the jumps from $15. Do not count $15 itself: that gives $6.

items.q: Benjamin buys a colouring book for $4. He pays with a $10 bill. How much change does he get?
items.e: Count up from $4 to $10: $4 + $6 = $10. The change is $6. Check: $4 + $6 = $10. Count the jumps from $4. Do not count $4 itself: that gives $7.

items.q: Liam buys a toque for $11. He pays with a $20 bill. How much change does he get?
items.e: Count up from $11 to $20: $11 + $9 = $20. The change is $9. Check: $11 + $9 = $20. Count the jumps from $11. Do not count $11 itself: that gives $10.

items.q: Sofia buys a book for $9 with a $20 bill. Is the change more or less than $10?
items.e: $9 is less than $10, so the change from $20 is more than $10. Exactly: $9 + $1 = $10, $10 + $10 = $20, so the change is $11. That is more than $10.

sets.title: Shopping problems: snack sale and book fair

items.q: At the school snack sale, Ava buys popcorn and a juice box. How much does she spend?
items.e: 35¢ + 50¢: 30¢ + 50¢ = 80¢, and 80¢ + 5¢ = 85¢. 15¢ is the difference, not the total.

items.q: At the snack sale, Kai buys a cookie and an apple. He pays with a loonie. How much change does he get?
items.e: Cost: 40¢ + 25¢ = 65¢. Count up from 65¢ to $1: 65¢ + 5¢ = 70¢, 70¢ + 30¢ = $1. Add the jumps: 5¢ + 30¢ = 35¢. The change is 35¢. 65¢ is the cost, not the change.

items.q: At the snack sale, a granola bar costs 45¢. Priya pays with 2 quarters. How much change does she get?
items.e: 2 quarters = 25¢ + 25¢ = 50¢. Count up: 45¢ + 5¢ = 50¢. The change is 5¢. 55¢ is the change from $1, but Priya paid only 50¢.

items.q: Olivia has 3 dimes and 2 nickels. She wants a granola bar for 45¢. Does she have enough money?
items.e: Dimes: 10¢, 20¢, 30¢. Nickels: 35¢, 40¢. Olivia has 40¢. 40¢ + 5¢ = 45¢, so no, she needs 5¢ more. 10¢ more comes from mixing up the dime and the nickel.

items.q: At the book fair, Emma buys a book and a poster. How much does she spend?
items.e: $8 + $4: $8 + $2 = $10, and $10 + $2 = $12. $4 is the difference, not the total.

items.q: At the book fair, Chloe buys a book and a poster. She pays with a $20 bill. How much change does she get?
items.e: Cost: $8 + $4 = $12. Count up from $12 to $20: $12 + $8 = $20. The change is $8. $12 is the cost, not the change.

items.q: At the book fair, bookmarks cost $2 each. Noah buys 3 bookmarks. How much does he pay?
items.e: 3 bookmarks: $2 + $2 + $2 = $6. $5 comes from adding 2 + 3. $4 is only 2 bookmarks.

items.q: Nathan has saved $15. He buys a book for $9. How much money is left?
items.e: Count up from $9 to $15: $9 + $1 = $10, $10 + $5 = $15. Add the jumps: $1 + $5 = $6. $6 is left. Check: $9 + $6 = $15. $24 adds instead of taking away.

items.q: Mateo wants a book that costs $12. He has $7. How much more money does he need?
items.e: Count up from $7 to $12: $7 + $3 = $10, $10 + $2 = $12. Add the jumps: $3 + $2 = $5. He needs $5 more. $19 adds the two amounts.

items.q: Mei has a loonie. Can she buy a juice box, popcorn and a cookie at the snack sale?
items.e: Estimate: 50¢ + 35¢ is already 85¢. Add 40¢ more and it is more than 100¢. So no, they cost more than $1 (but less than $2).

items.q: For the Terry Fox Run, Amira brings these coins to give. How much does she give?
items.e: Loonies: $1, $2, $3. Four quarters make $1. $3 + $1 = $4. $7 counts every coin as $1. $3 forgets the quarters.

items.q: At the snack sale, Leah buys a muffin for 75¢ with a loonie. How much change does she get?
items.e: Count up from 75¢ to $1: 75¢ + 5¢ = 80¢, 80¢ + 20¢ = $1. Add the jumps: 5¢ + 20¢ = 25¢. The change is 25¢, one quarter.

items.q: At the book fair, a poster costs $4. Arjun pays with a $5 bill. How much change does he get?
items.e: Count up: $4 + $1 = $5. The change is $1, one loonie. $9 adds instead of taking away.

items.q: At the snack sale, cookies cost 40¢ each. Maya buys 2 cookies and pays with a loonie. How much change does she get?
items.e: 2 cookies: 40¢ + 40¢ = 80¢. Count up: 80¢ + 20¢ = $1. The change is 20¢. 60¢ is the change for only 1 cookie.

items.q: At the book fair, Jayden buys 2 chapter books for $6 each. He pays with a $20 bill. How much change does he get?
items.e: Cost: $6 + $6 = $12. Count up from $12 to $20: $12 + $8 = $20. The change is $8. $14 is the change for only 1 book.

items.q: Zoe has a $10 bill and a toonie. She buys a book for $9. How much money does she have left?
items.e: A $10 bill and a toonie make $12. Count up: $9 + $1 = $10, $10 + $2 = $12. $3 is left. $1 forgets the toonie.

items.q: Pizza Day is every Friday. A slice costs $2. Owen buys a slice every Friday for 4 weeks. How much does he spend?
items.e: $2, $4, $6, $8. 4 slices cost $8. $6 comes from adding 2 + 4. $10 would be 5 weeks.

items.q: The class field trip to the science centre costs $15. Hana pays with a $20 bill. How much change does she get?
items.e: Count up from $15 to $20: $15 + $5 = $20. The change is $5. Check: $15 + $5 = $20.

items.q: Ethan buys an orange for 60¢ and pays with a loonie. Which coins could be the change?
For a class snack sale, Aiden’s class sells freezies for 50¢ each. They sell 6 freezies. How much money do they make?
items.e: Two freezies make $1. 6 freezies make 3 pairs, so $1 + $1 + $1 = $3. 56¢ adds 50 + 6. $6 counts each freezie as $1.
